title: ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
inspection: Primary abstract and benchmark authors' repository/landing page; not full-paper audit
finding: Its scientific workflow tasks score programs, execution and costs. This supports distinguishing component execution from original discovery and motivates recording expenditure.
limit: A historical benchmark and its model results do not predict Astra performance. No benchmark percentage is adopted as an Astra estimate.

title: When Debate Helps: Proposal Supply and Verification-Aware Readout in Multi-Agent Reasoning
finding: Separates complementary proposal supply from selecting a correct proposal. This suggests studying distinct failure coverage rather than agent count alone.
limit: A recent preprint on bounded reasoning benchmarks, including multiple choice; the authors explicitly limit generalization to open-ended outputs. It does not validate an Astra coordination policy.

title: Accelerating science with human-aware artificial intelligence
finding: Distinguishes forecasting what researchers will discover from exploring hypotheses outside current researcher crowds. This motivates testing whether Astra merely follows densely represented existing agendas.
limit: Prediction of later literature and generation of unusual hypotheses are not established useful breakthroughs. Its reported gains are not Astra gains.

title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists
inspection: Primary abstract, counterfactual framework, recommendations and limitations
finding: Tests answers when evidence is preserved, withdrawn or reversed, because static correct answers can come from prior knowledge. This directly challenges the meaning of a high static score in the present cue-rich pilot.
limit: Recent preprint with small scientific task sets; evidence responsiveness is necessary but insufficient for scientific quality. The present pilot did not perform its withdrawal/reversal test.

title: TruthInsightBench: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Automated Evaluation of Open-Ended Scientific Discovery Agents
finding: Withholds source conclusions and analysis paths and scores the maturity of claims, rather than treating recovery of a hidden target study as discovery.
limit: Its LLM adjudication and benchmark performance were not independently audited here. It is a design reference, not proof that its scoring transfers to Astra.

title: Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology
inspection: Primary publication abstract via PubMed; full text fetch failed
finding: Reports an association between smaller human teams and disruptive work, motivating attention to protected question ownership.
limit: Human-team observational association does not establish the optimal number, topology or interruption policy for AI workers. It does not justify reducing Astra's pool.
